summary.headline: Sterling Tools standalone fasteners grew total income 23.7% to INR201.9 crore with PAT up 48.4%, while EV subsidiaries remain loss-making until FY28 breakeven.
summary.overview: Standalone fasteners delivered Q1 FY27 total income of INR201.9 crore (+23.7% YoY), EBITDA of INR31.1 crore (+26.9%, margin 15.4% vs 15%) and PAT of INR16.4 crore (+48.4%, margin 8.1%). Management flagged steel and broader inflation (chemicals, tungsten, wages up to 35% in some areas) as cost pressures, with pass-through price negotiations at a mature stage and expected to hit P&L after a 2-4 month lag. Subsidiaries SEM and STML continue to lose money; both are guided to break even in FY28 at combined revenue of about INR225-250 crore. Capacity utilisation is 90-95% and an INR88 crore fasteners capex (misstated as INR80 crore on the call) is mostly expected to commission in H2 FY27.

financial_highlights.change: EBITDA margin up only ~40 bps per analyst

segments.name: Standalone fasteners
segments.commentary: Total income INR201.9 crore (+23.7%), EBITDA INR31.1 crore (15.4% margin), PAT INR16.4 crore (8.1% margin); management says growth is outpacing the auto industry, with 20%+ growth in Q1 and similar near-term run-rate expected.

segments.name: Sterling E-Mobility (SEM)
segments.commentary: Loss-making; FY25 revenue was about INR380 crore on one anchor customer that in-sourced, a drop of about INR280 crore. Breakeven guided at about INR175 crore revenue in FY28; current capacity over INR300 crore; 33 active programs and 4 OEM business confirmations. Revenue mix planned at 30-35% two/three-wheeler and about 65% commercial vehicles.

segments.name: Sterling Tech-Mobility (STML)
segments.commentary: Pre-commercial; HV DC contactors and relays. Seven customer programs secured; commercial supplies to start Q2 FY27. Breakeven guided at about INR70 crore revenue in FY28; current capacity about INR140 crore on 3-shift basis. Testing/validation takes 8-16 months per customer.

guidance_outlook: Fasteners: management expects to hold margin structures on a full-year basis despite steel and inflation, citing customer price increases at an advanced stage.
Fasteners: near-term growth expected similar to Q1's 20%+ pace, unless the auto industry slows.
EV businesses (SEM and STML) revenue growth guided at 20-30% in FY27 and 30-40% in FY28.
SEM and STML both expected to break even in FY28; both will lose money in FY27.
Long-term EBITDA/operating margin for SEM and STML targeted at about 10%, plus or minus 2%, at breakeven scale.
Fasteners capex: INR88 crore in FY27, with a further INR25-30 crore next year to support about INR1,000 crore potential revenue, if markets support.
capex_capacity: Fasteners capex INR88 crore (stated as INR80 crore in the call, corrected by management), purely expansion of existing facilities in Bangalore and two NCR plants; some capacity kicked in marginally in Q1, bulk in H2 FY27.

SEM onboard charger and multifunction unit lines to be commissioned by end of Q2 FY27; samples then need about 4 months of on-road trials (around 50,000 km), so supplies expected around December 2026 or January 2027.
STML fully automated facility in Bangalore; current capacity about INR140 crore on 3-shift basis; commercial supplies from Q2 FY27.
SEM current capacity over INR300 crore without further investment.
Total invested capital in subsidiaries about INR100 crore (STML about INR50 crore, SEM about INR48-49 crore).
demand_pricing: Steel price increases in Q1 created cost pressure; lower-cost inventory largely consumed, so impact expected to be more visible in the coming quarter.
Steel pass-through negotiations typically take 2-4 months; management says customers are positive on compensating for inflation this year.
Industry: PV sales +25.9% to 1.27 million, 2W +20.3% to 5.63 million, CV +18.3%, 3W +29.7% YoY in Q1 FY27 per management.
SEM: LCV, HCV and public transport bus programs gaining traction; EV demand supported by high oil prices.
Integrated units for heavy bus and truck platforms priced at about INR3-3.5 lakh per unit.
Two new 2-wheeler programs at advanced stage with one OEM response expected in coming months; management sees second-sourcing opportunity at incumbents.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin rise about 270 bps while EBITDA margin rose only about 40 bps in standalone?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited steel price increases plus broad inflation (chemicals, tungsten, minimum wages up to 35% in some areas), partly offset by shop-floor efficiencies.

qa_highlights.question: What is the fasteners capacity utilisation and when will new capex be commissioned?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation at 90-95%, described as fully utilised given product mix; most of the INR88 crore capex expected to commission in H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How should standalone EBITDA margin be considered for the rest of FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not expect EBITDA to weaken further and expects to hold full-year margin structures, based on price increases at an advanced stage.

qa_highlights.question: What are breakeven levels and timeline for SEM and STML?
qa_highlights.answer: Both expected to break even in FY28; SEM at about INR175 crore revenue and STML at about INR70 crore, combined about INR225-250 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is peak revenue capacity of the subsidiaries?
qa_highlights.answer: SEM over INR300 crore and STML about INR140 crore on current capacity, total about INR440 crore (corrected from INR400 crore plus).

qa_highlights.question: Will the fasteners capex take capacity to INR1,000 crore revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, if markets support it, with a further INR25-30 crore of investment next year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the new SEM onboard charger and multifunction line contributing soon?
qa_highlights.answer: Lines commissioned by end of Q2; customer trials of about 4 months mean supplies around December 2026 or January 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Why is SEM loss-making and what is the R&D spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Loss due to revenue collapse after anchor customer in-sourcing (FY25 revenue of about INR380 crore falling by about INR280 crore) and continuing R&D; about 130 people, more than half in product or application engineering.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ADAS regulatory opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Regulation for medium and heavy CVs, about 0.5 million units a year, from October 2027, possibly pushed to January 2028; a Chinese partner signed.

risks_watch: Steel and inflation pass-through: lower-cost inventory largely consumed, so steel cost impact expected to be more visible next quarter; pass-through takes 2-4 months to reach P&L
Gross margin rose about 270 bps but EBITDA margin only about 40 bps; watch whether full-year standalone margin holds as management expects
Capex timing: most of the INR88 crore fasteners capex is expected to commission in H2 FY27, so benefits are back-ended
Subsidiary losses continue through FY27 for SEM and STML; breakeven depends on FY28 revenue reaching about INR225-250 crore combined
SEM onboard charger and multifunction lines due by end Q2 FY27; customer on-road trials of about 4 months put supplies around Dec 2026 or Jan 2027
STML testing and validation of 8-16 months per customer; commercial supplies from Q2 FY27 remain subject to certification timelines
key_quotes: So we are at a very mature stage of negotiations for price increases on account of steel.

We hope -- despite the pressures, we are quite confident that we'll be able to hold our margin structures on a full year basis despite the steel and inflation because we expect to get price increases from customers, which are in a very advanced stage.
So it's going to be slow.
So basically, both businesses put together, about INR340 crores revenue is the current capacity installed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the standalone fasteners business, its margins and pricing outlook, and on near-term 20%+ growth. More cautious and evasive on subsidiary timelines, repeatedly stressing that the EV ecosystem is slow and that breakeven and growth depend on customer validation and market support.
